findings.description: In async `retry_any.__ror__`, the flatten check tests `isinstance(other, retry_all)` where it should test `retry_any`. This is the wrong class, and it is inconsistent with the sync version in tenacity/retry.py.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `retry_all(a, b) | async_retry_any(c, d)`. The check matches, so the result is `retry_any(a, b, c, d)`, which turns an AND group into an OR. Behavior changes silently, and a retry fires when only `a` is true. The same mistake appears in the sync `retry_any.__ror__`, which should check `retry_any`.

findings.description: In `retry_any.__ror__`, the flatten check tests `isinstance(other, retry_any)`. When `other` is a `retry_all`, this check does not match, which is correct. But the async variant on line 112 has the wrong class.
findings.rationale: This sync check is correct, so no defect is reported here and the confidence is low.

findings.description: The async `retry_all.__rand__` flatten check is consistent with the sync version.
